workflows.title: How to correct how a policy's sections were parsed
workflows.purpose: Fix mis-parsed section headings from an uploaded policy document, including reordering hierarchy or merging sections, applied for all future versions.
steps: Navigate to Testing program > Policies
Click the row-actions button (ellipsis icon) for the policy whose sections need correcting
Click "Update sections" in the dropdown menu
In the "Update sections" dialog, tick the checkbox next to the section(s) that were parsed incorrectly
Optionally shift-click a further-down row to select every section in between
Click "Shift left" to promote the selected section(s) up a hierarchy level, or "Shift right" to demote them under the section above
Alternatively, click "Merge up" to fold the selected section(s) into the section immediately above them
Alternatively, hover a single row and click its inline chevron-left, chevron-right, or merge (up-arrow) icon to shift or merge just that one section
If needed, click "Undo" or "Redo" to step back and forth through the corrections made so far
Click "Save corrections" to persist the changes; they are kept with the policy and re-applied to every future version uploaded

workflows.title: How to log a check manually in the Check Blotter
workflows.purpose: Manually record a single client check received and forwarded, with automatic duplicate detection before the record is saved.
steps: Navigate to People oversight > Check blotter
Click "Log check" in the top-right of the toolbar to open the Log check dialog.
Confirm the "Manual entry" tab is selected (it is the default; "Bulk upload" is the other option).
If you have permission to log on behalf of others, use the "Representative" field to search and select the employee the check is for.
Enter the check amount in the "Amount" field (must be greater than zero).
Enter the client or issuing party's name in the "Issuer" field.
Enter the account holder or firm name in the "Payee" field.
Click the "Date received" field and select the date the check was received from the calendar picker.
Click the "Date forwarded" field and select the date the check was forwarded (a "Late submission" warning appears automatically if more than 1 business day elapsed between the two dates).
Enter where the check was sent in the "Forwarded to" field.
Optionally enter the check number in the "Check #" field.
Click "Log check" to submit — the system automatically runs a duplicate check based on matching representative, amount, date received, and check number.
If a duplicate is detected, review the "Duplicate entry" warning and either click "Log check anyways" to save it regardless, or click "Cancel" to discard.
If no duplicate is found, the check is saved automatically and the dialog closes, adding the new record to the Check blotter table.

workflows.title: How to close a check as compliant or non-compliant
workflows.purpose: Open a logged check record in the Check blotter and resolve it by marking it Compliant or Non-compliant with an optional or required resolution note.
steps: Navigate to People oversight > Check blotter
Click on a check record row in the list to open its detail view.

In the top action bar of the check detail view, confirm the check is resolvable: if it is archived or has been escalated to another admin, the "Compliant" and "Non-compliant" buttons will be disabled with a tooltip explaining why.
To close as compliant, click the "Compliant" button (shield-check icon) in the top action bar.
In the "Close as compliant" dialog, optionally enter a note in the "Resolution note (Optional)" field, e.g. "Approved by compliance review."
Click "Save" to resolve and stay on the same check, or click "Save & next" (or "Save & Close" if this is the last item in the list) to resolve and automatically advance to the next check.
To close as non-compliant instead, click the "Non-compliant" button (shield-ban icon) in the top action bar.
In the "Close as non-compliant" dialog, enter a note in the "Resolution note (Required)" field, e.g. "Violation of 24h rule confirmed." — the Save buttons stay disabled until this field is filled in.
Click "Save" to resolve and stay on the same check, or click "Save & next" / "Save & Close" to resolve and advance.

Confirm the resolution: a success toast reading "Check resolved." appears, and the check's status badge updates to reflect the compliant or non-compliant outcome; the note is also recorded in the check's audit trail.

Click "Next: Termination information" to proceed to Step 3

Select the "Date terminated (MM/DD/YYYY)" using the date picker

Click "Next: Disclosures" to proceed to Step 4

In the Individual acknowledgment and consent section, confirm the printed name and signing date, check "Electronic signature of individual", then click "Sign individual acknowledgment"
Navigate to the filing detail page and click "Validate filing" to run FINRA validation

workflows.title: How to complete and submit a branch exam task questionnaire

workflows.title: How to add a dataset of filtered communications to a case

workflows.title: How to upload reviewed emails to test an AI compliance subrule

workflows.title: How to configure document expiration and renewal rules in Marketing
workflows.purpose: Configure firm-wide and document-type expiration periods, automatic renewal or resubmission rules, and expiration notification schedules for marketing documents.
steps: Navigate to Marketing > Expiration dates
Toggle on "Firm-wide expiration" to enable default document expiration across the firm.
Enter the expiration timeframe in the "Default expiration" field, and set the lead times in "Near-expiration badge" and "Near-expiration notification".
Select the expiry behavior by toggling "Renew it automatically" or "Resubmit it for a new approval".
If resubmission is chosen, specify the number of days and timing in the "Resubmit [N] days [before/after] the expiration date." row.
Click "Add document type override" to configure custom rules for a specific document type.
In the "Add document type override" dialog, select an option from the "Document type" dropdown, enter the duration in "Expires after", and click "Add override".

In the "Expiration by document type" table, configure "Auto-renew" or "Auto-resubmit" per document type, and toggle "Per-document overrides" to allow individual document owners to manage resubmission.

In the "Expiration notifications" card, switch the "Enable" toggle on, and select the recipient checkboxes ("Admin", "Approver", and/or "Submitter") for "Expiration approaching" and "Document expired".
Click "Save changes" to persist all expiration and renewal configuration settings.

Enter the detailed background text, compliance guidance, or required disclaimer copy in the "Content" field

workflows.title: How to create a new marketing project

Click "Next" to advance to the "Add documents" sub-step.
Drag files into the upload dropzone (or use the file picker) to attach documents; the panel shows the guidance "Upload up to [N] files, up to [size] each ([total] total)".

Click "Next" to advance to "Workflow setup" (labeled "Routing questions" if the company uses a routing questionnaire) and select the appropriate workflow or answer the routing questions (Yes/No or multiple-choice options).
Click "Next" to advance to "Submission questions" and answer any required questions (marked with *).
Click "Next" (header tab "Upload") to move to the "Upload documents" main step and review/complete document details for each uploaded file.
Click "Next" to reach the "Save project" step and review the project details, documents, and routing/workflow summary.
Click "Create project" in the header to submit the project (or click "Save as draft" to save progress without submitting, or "Cancel" to discard).

Toggle on "Firm-wide expiration" to enable firm-wide default expiration

workflows.title: How to claim and approve a marketing document
workflows.purpose: Claim an unclaimed marketing submission from the tier review queue and approve the document after completing compliance review.
steps: Navigate to Marketing > Dashboard
In the "Unclaimed in my tier" table, locate the marketing submission awaiting review and click "Claim"
In the "Claim review" dialog, click "Claim review" to assign the document to yourself
In the "Documents assigned to me" table, locate the claimed document and click "Review"
Inspect the document preview, metadata, and flagged compliance checklist items
Click "Approve" in the review action bar
In the "Approve document" dialog, enter any compliance notes in the "Comments" field and specify the approval period in "Valid for"
Click "Approve" to finalize the approval and update the document status to Approved

workflows.title: How to configure project submission questions
workflows.purpose: Configure submitter answering frequency and build custom questionnaires required when submitting marketing materials.
steps: Navigate to Marketing > Settings
Click the "Submission questions" tab
Under "How submitters answer", select a frequency radio option ("Let the submitter choose", "Once per project", or "Once per document")
Click "Edit" (or "Create questionnaire" if setting up a questionnaire for the first time)
Click "Add question" to append a new question card
Enter the prompt text in "Question label" and select the answer format from the "Question type" dropdown ("Date", "Single select", "Multi select", or "Long text")
For "Single select" or "Multi select" types, click "Add option" and enter the choice name in "Value"
Optionally toggle "Required" to make an answer mandatory, or toggle "Conditional" and click "Add condition" to define display rules based on previous questions
Click "Save questionnaire" to persist your questionnaire configuration

workflows.title: How to add a new document to an existing marketing project
workflows.purpose: Upload and attach a new document to an existing marketing project for compliance review.
steps: Navigate to Marketing > Projects
Click on the target marketing project from the list to open its project details page
Locate the "Documents" section on the project details page
Click "Add document" to open the document upload modal
Click the file upload area or drag and drop your file into "Upload file"
Enter the file name in "Document title"
Select the collateral category from the "Document type" dropdown
Click "Upload" to confirm and add the document to the project
Verify the new document is listed under "Documents" with its initial status

workflows.title: How to configure comment templates for document review
workflows.purpose: Create and manage reusable comment templates to streamline feedback and annotations during marketing document reviews.
steps: Navigate to Marketing > Settings
Click the "Comment templates" tab
Click "Add template" to open the template dialog
Enter a descriptive name for the template in the "Title" field
Enter the reusable review feedback text in the "Body" field
Click "Save" to add the template to the local list
(Optional) Click the pencil icon next to an existing template to modify its "Title" or "Body", then click "Save"
(Optional) Click the trash icon next to an existing template to delete it from the list
Click "Save changes" in the upper right corner to persist the comment templates

workflows.title: How to configure marketing document types
workflows.purpose: Configure, create, toggle, and manage custom document type categories available for marketing project submissions.
steps: Navigate to Marketing > Settings
Select the "Document types" tab.
Click "Add document type" to open the creation dialog.
Enter the name of the new category in the "Document type" input field.
Click "Add type" to add the document type to the library.
Toggle the active switch in any document type's row to enable or disable it for marketing submissions.
Click the actions menu on an existing custom document type row to access management options.
Select "Edit", update the name in the "Document type" field, and click "Save changes".
Select "Delete" for an unused custom type and confirm by clicking "Delete type" in the confirmation dialog.
Click "Save changes" in the page header to persist all document type configurations.

workflows.title: How to move a project card through the review kanban board
workflows.purpose: Review and approve marketing materials within a project to advance its card through the kanban review stages.
steps: Navigate to Marketing > Projects & Documents
Click "Projects" to display the review kanban board view.
Under the "For my attention" column, locate the project card that needs review.
Click the project card or open its "..." actions menu and select "View" to enter the review workspace.
Review the submitted materials and flags, then click "Approve document" in the upper action toolbar.
In the "Approve document" confirmation dialog, enter any optional review notes in the "Comments" field.
Click "Approve document" to confirm your decision and advance the project's workflow status.
Click "Back to projects" to return to the kanban board and confirm the card has moved from "For my attention" to "Resolved".

workflows.title: How to add context to Firm Intelligence
workflows.purpose: Ask a natural-language question against firm context and receive a sourced answer, saved as a chat thread.
steps: Navigate to Marketing > Intelligence
Enter your question in the prompt textarea (e.g. "What's our policy on accepting gifts from clients?")
Click "Submit" (the up-arrow send button) to send the question — or press Enter
Wait for the app to create a new chat and post your question as the first turn — you are redirected automatically to the new chat thread
Review the sourced answer rendered in the chat transcript, shown as an assistant finding card with citations
Optionally click "Save context" on the answer card to persist the finding, if it is not already completed
Ask a follow-up question in the thread composer to continue the conversation, which is saved to the same chat thread

workflows.title: How to edit or manage a Firm Intelligence finding
workflows.purpose: Review, edit, confirm, or delete findings extracted from source documents in Firm Intelligence.
steps: Navigate to Marketing > Intelligence
Click "Manage context" to open the context management page.
Click the source document accordion row to expand its extracted findings.
Click the view icon on the target finding row to open the finding details drawer.
Click "Edit" in the finding details drawer to open the "Edit finding" dialog.
Update the title and edit the finding text in the content field.
Click "Save changes" to update the finding.
Alternatively, click "Save Context" to confirm and accept a finding awaiting review.
To remove an unwanted finding, click "Delete", then click "Delete" in the "Delete finding?" confirmation dialog.

workflows.title: How to save and reuse a custom trade search
workflows.purpose: Configure custom trade filters on the trade blotter and save them as a named search to quickly reapply the same criteria later.
steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Trades
Click "Filter" to open the trade filter options.
Set your desired filter criteria (such as date range, symbol, transaction type, or account) and click "Apply".
Click "Save search" next to the active filters.
Enter a descriptive name for your search in the "Search name" field.
Click "Save" to store the custom trade search.
To reuse the search, click the "Saved searches" dropdown menu above the trade table.
Select the saved search name from the list to instantly reapply all saved filter parameters.

workflows.title: How to manually run a surveillance rule in Account surveillance
workflows.purpose: Trigger an on-demand execution of an account surveillance rule for a specified date range and review the generated results.
steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Rule library
Locate the target surveillance rule in the table, or find it using the "Search rules" input field
Click the row actions menu ("...") on the target rule and select "Run now"
In the "Run rule" dialog, select the evaluation window from the "Date range" dropdown (or enter "Start date" and "End date")
Confirm the target scope under "Accounts" (e.g. "All accounts" or selected accounts)
Click "Run rule" to initiate the surveillance run
Confirm the "Rule run queued" toast notification appears
Review the resulting execution under the "Rule runs" tab or on the rule run results page to inspect the processing "Status" and flagged alerts

workflows.title: How to reopen a closed exception in Account surveillance
workflows.purpose: Filter for closed exceptions, open the exception details, and submit a reopening reason to restore it to the open queue.
steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Exceptions
Click the "Status" filter dropdown above the exceptions table.
Select "Closed" from the status options.
Click on the closed exception row you wish to reopen to open its details panel.
Click "Reopen exception" in the action header.
Enter an explanation in the "Reason for reopening" field.
Click "Reopen" to confirm and return the exception to the open queue.

workflows.title: How to export trade data in Account surveillance
workflows.purpose: Export filtered or complete trade blotter records from Account surveillance to a CSV file for compliance reviews and reporting.
steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Trades
Optionally click "Filters" to narrow down the trade blotter by date range, account number, or review status.
Click "Export" located in the action bar above the trades table.
Select "Export to CSV" from the export options dropdown.
Click "Download" to export and save the trade records file to your local computer.

workflows.title: How to archive a flagged exception in Account surveillance
workflows.purpose: Archive a flagged exception in Account surveillance to remove it from the active review queue while maintaining an audit trail.
steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Exceptions
Select the "Flagged" tab to view all unresolved exceptions.
Click on the flagged exception row to open the exception details pane.
Click "Archive" in the action header.
In the "Archive exception" dialog, enter an explanation in "Reason for archiving".
Click "Archive" to confirm and remove the item from the active queue.
Click the "Archived" tab to verify that the exception is now recorded in the archive list.

workflows.title: How to escalate a flagged compliance exception
workflows.purpose: Escalate a flagged compliance exception in Account surveillance to a supervisor or senior compliance officer with an escalation rationale and assignment.
steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Exceptions
Locate and click on the flagged exception record in the table to open the exception details drawer.
Click "Escalate" in the review actions panel.
In the "Escalate exception" dialog, click the "Assign to" dropdown and select the designated reviewer.
Enter the compliance justification in the "Reason" field.
Enter any supporting context or findings in the "Notes" text box.
Click "Escalate exception" to submit the escalation and update the status badge to "Escalated".

workflows.title: How to close a flagged compliance exception
workflows.purpose: Review and close a flagged account or trade surveillance exception by documenting a compliance determination and resolution notes.
steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Exceptions
Click on the flagged exception row in the active exceptions table to open the details panel.
Review the triggered surveillance rule, transaction details, and compliance risk analysis.
Click "Resolve exception" in the top action bar.
Select the resolution outcome from the "Determination" dropdown (e.g., "No violation / False positive" or "Resolved with rep").
Enter the compliance justification and audit trail rationale in the "Resolution notes" field.
Click "Close exception" to confirm the resolution and move the item to the closed queue.

workflows.title: How to bulk close multiple flagged exceptions at once
workflows.purpose: An admin selects several flagged exceptions in the alerts table and closes them all together after entering a single audit reason.
steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Overview

Optionally use the filter chips ("High risk", "Medium risk", "Low risk", "New", "Under review", "Resolved", "Escalated", "Assigned to me", "Sandbox") or the "Filter by rule" dropdown to narrow down the flags you want to close.
In the table header row, click the header checkbox to select all flags on the current page, or click the row checkbox next to each individual flag you want to close.
In the bulk action bar that appears above the table showing the selected count (e.g. "3 flags selected"), click "Close".
In the "Close flags" confirmation dialog, enter a summary in the "Reason" textarea (this is required and stored in the audit record for each flag).
Click "Close <count> flags" to confirm.
Wait for the dialog to close and the selection to clear — the closed flags now show a "Resolved" status badge in the table.

workflows.title: How to import trade and holdings data
workflows.purpose: Select a custodian and upload a CSV or XLSX file containing trades and holdings for automated surveillance processing.
steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Import data
Click the "Select a custodian" dropdown to view available custodians
Select the custodian matching your source file from the dropdown list
Click the "Input CSV/XLSX" file upload area to choose a file from your computer
Select the .csv or .xlsx file containing your trade and holdings records
Click "Upload and Proceed" to submit the data file for ingestion
Confirm the "Upload successful" toast notification indicating your trades and holdings are processing

workflows.title: How to create a new surveillance rule from a template
workflows.purpose: Browse surveillance rule templates and configure detection thresholds, accounts, and severity using the rule creation wizard.
steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Overview
Click "Rule library" to open the surveillance rules page.
Click "Create new rule" to browse available templates.
On the "Select a rule template" page, locate your target template card (such as "Front running", "Wash trading", or "Churning") and click "Use this template".
In the "Name & overview" step of the wizard, enter a name in "Rule name" and an optional description in "Description".
Click "Next" to advance through "Detection parameters", "Security matching", and "Pattern & escalation" to set your detection window and thresholds.
In the "Accounts & groups" step, configure target accounts or search specific groups to exclude, then click "Next".
In the "Activation & severity" step, select an activation option (e.g. "Activate on publish") and choose a severity level (e.g. "Moderate").
Click "Next" to reach "Review & publish", verify the rule summary, and click "Publish".

workflows.title: How to edit a surveillance rule's configuration
workflows.purpose: Open an existing surveillance rule and update its detection parameters, severity level, and threshold configurations.
steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Rules
Locate the surveillance rule you wish to configure and click "Edit" on its row.
In the rule configuration panel, update the rule details such as "Rule name", "Description", or "Severity".
Adjust the template-specific detection parameters and thresholds under "Parameters" (e.g., lookback windows or threshold amounts).
Toggle "Active" to enable or disable rule enforcement as needed.
Click "Save changes" to apply the updated configuration.

workflows.title: How to activate, deactivate, or sandbox a surveillance rule
workflows.purpose: Toggle a surveillance rule between active, inactive, and sandbox deployment statuses to manage alert generation.
steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Rule library
Locate the target rule row in the table and check its current state in the "Status" column
Click the "..." actions menu button on the right side of the rule row
To enable an inactive or sandboxed rule, click "Activate" in the dropdown menu
To deactivate or sandbox an active rule, click "Deactivate" in the dropdown menu to open the "Deactivate Rule" dialog
In the "Deactivate Rule" modal, choose either "Inactive" to turn off evaluations completely or "Sandbox" to test silently without generating alerts
Click "Confirm" to apply the selected status, or click "Cancel" to close the dialog without changes
Verify the updated status badge in the "Status" column, or filter by the "Active", "Sandbox", or "Inactive" tabs above the table

workflows.purpose: Queue an on-demand run of a rule outside its normal schedule and view the resulting rule run.
steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Rule library
Click the row actions menu (kebab icon) for the target rule in the rules table
Click "Run now" in the dropdown menu
Wait for the "Rule run queued" confirmation toast confirming the run was queued
You are automatically redirected to the new rule run's results page
Review the rule run results, including its processing status and alerts, on the "<Rule name> - Results" page

workflows.title: How to view a rule run's results
workflows.purpose: Inspect the status, execution metrics, and generated alerts of a specific rule run in Account surveillance.
steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Rules
In the rules table, locate the target rule and click the timestamp displayed in the "Last run" column to open its execution results
Review the run overview header to verify the run's "Status" badge, "Start date/time", and "End date/time"
Inspect the summary metric cards to confirm the number of records evaluated and total "Alerts" generated

workflows.title: How to build and manage client-company relationships
workflows.purpose: Visualize client, representative, and account ownership hierarchies and link entities together using the interactive relationship graph.
steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Company structure
Wait for the graph canvas to load until the "Loading relationship data..." indicator disappears and the "Client Relationship Builder" workspace is visible.
Use the bottom-left ReactFlow navigation controls to zoom or fit the view to locate the desired source and target entity nodes.
Locate the circular connection handle on the source entity node (e.g. representative or client).
Click and hold the source node handle, then drag the connecting edge across to the target node handle (e.g. client or account).
Release the connection line onto the target handle to create the new relationship.
Verify that the "Creating relationship..." status indicator displays in the bottom-right corner while the relationship is being saved.
Confirm the newly created relationship edge renders on the canvas with its assigned relationship label (such as "OWNS" or "MANAGES").

workflows.title: How to search and filter representatives
workflows.purpose: Search representatives by first or last name and filter the roster by active or inactive status.
steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Representatives
Enter a representative's name into the "Search first or last name..." field
Click the "Active" filter chip to view only active representatives
Click the "Inactive" filter chip to view only inactive representatives
Click the "All statuses" filter chip to clear the status filter and show all representatives
Click the clear icon in the "Search first or last name..." input to reset the search query

workflows.title: How to monitor incoming data feed sync status
workflows.purpose: Review and filter incoming custodian data feed syncs by source, status, and file type to identify failed or delayed imports.
steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Feed monitor
Enter a search term in the "Search" input field to filter syncs by source, status, or filename
Click the "All sources" dropdown and select a specific data feed source to quickly narrow down the list
Click "Filters" to open the "Feed filters" drawer
In the "Feed filters" drawer, select one or more checkboxes under "Source" to filter by custodian or data feed provider
Under "Status", select checkboxes such as "Failed" or "Delayed" to isolate problematic syncs
Under "File type", select the relevant file format checkboxes to filter by imported data type
Click "Search" in the drawer to apply the selected filters and update the data feed list
Review the table columns including "Source", "Sync date", "Status", "File type", and "Filename" to evaluate feed health
Click "Clear all" to reset all applied filters and display all data feed sync records
